École Hélène-Boullé is a francophone public elementary school of the Centre de services scolaire
de Montréal (CSSDM) in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, in a 1927-28 building at the corner
of avenue de Gaspé and rue Gounod. This report describes it in three layers: the school itself,
the kilometre around it, and what a three-bedroom home there costs to buy or rent this month. It
is one output of MTL-101, which works backwards from the school to the neighbourhood.

Four nearby schools carry through the tables as comparators: **Sainte-Cécile**, 984 m south on the
same avenue, which has [its own report](villeray-petite-patrie-report.qmd); **Marie-Favery** and
**Saint-Gabriel-Lalemant**, both in Villeray; and **Saint-Arsène**, across the borough line in
Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie. Each of the five has its own section below, because the zone tables
describe kilometres and say nothing about the school standing in the middle of one — and on that
score the five differ more than their overlapping circles suggest.

::: {.callout-important}
## Not a ranking

Each zone metric is shown with its decile among the 229 francophone public elementary schools on
the island outside the West Island, marked [d1]{.decile-low} to [d3]{.decile-low} for the lowest
three tenths, [d4]{.decile-mid} to [d7]{.decile-mid} for the middle, and [d8]{.decile-high} to
[d10]{.decile-high} for the top three. A high decile means a high value, nothing
more, so the label says which way is favourable for a family: ▲ higher is favourable (children,
parks, stations), ▼ lower is favourable (crime, collisions, deprivation, cost), and rows with no
glyph are descriptive. On the ▲ and ▼ rows the most favourable of the compared zones is [shaded]{.best}.
The report computes no composite score, and the IMSE is a socioeconomic index of the pupils enrolled,
not a measure of academic performance.
:::

# The schools

Five schools carry through this report. Hélène-Boullé is the subject; the other four are
comparators, and each gets its own section here because a zone table says nothing about the school
standing in it. Four of the five are ordinary neighbourhood schools taking pupils by address, with
the CSSDM's *libre choix* applying only if places remain; Saint-Arsène is the exception, carrying a
selective *élève-athlète* stream alongside its regular programme.

Every one of the five school websites returns HTTP 403 to anything that is not a browser, as most
`cssdm.gouv.qc.ca` school sites do. Facts drawn from their indexed pages rather than from a page
that loaded are marked *unverified* throughout.

## A full school, an expansion already built, and a gymnasium still waiting

The CSSDM's triennial plan for 2025-2028 states plainly that *"l'école occupe la totalité de
l'immeuble"* — the school has its whole building, so there is no relocation and no shared site to
weigh. What the same entry shows is a school at exactly 100% occupancy: 17 classes and 351 pupils
against a capacity of 391 places, with the plan's own forecasts easing to 14 classes and 315
pupils by 2027-2028.[^ptrdi]

That fullness has a history. Earlier CSSDM plans describe an expansion of eight to ten classrooms
and a gymnasium delivered around 2020-22, the documents disagreeing on the count, and a phased
masonry and window renovation of the rear façade across 2023 and 2024 (*unverified*: from search
extracts of the plans, not pages opened here). The gymnasium is the part that did not happen. The
CSSDM's funding page lists *"Ajout d'un gymnase (primaire)"* for Hélène-Boullé as **"non retenu au
PQI 2024-2034"** and then **"déposé de nouveau au PQI 2025-2035"**; the triennial plan adds that
the request went back to the ministry in autumn 2024. The school does not appear in the
PQI 2026-2036 list, and neither page says why, so the project's current status is genuinely
unresolved here rather than simply unknown to the agent.[^financement][^ptrdi]

This matters to a parent mainly as a question to ask: a full school with no gym of its own is the
single thing the public record flags about Hélène-Boullé.
:::

## The annexe: phase one done, phase two waiting on the ministry

The CSSDM's project sheet for the annexe records that phase one, selective interior demolition, is
complete, and that the service centre is seeking ministry funding for phase two: **eight added
classrooms**, renovation of the existing ones, a *carrefour d'apprentissage*, a multipurpose room
and a motor-skills room, and a regreened schoolyard, for a stated capacity of **184 pupils** and an
investment of **13.9 M$**. The schedule is given only as *"à venir"*, and the sheet was last
modified on 6 February 2024, so its current state is not established here.[^sgl-projet]

This is the second of the five schools whose published building file ends in a funding request
rather than a date — Hélène-Boullé's gymnasium is the other.
:::

## What the indices say

The MEQ's IMSE places the five schools in deciles 5 (Hélène-Boullé), 3 (Sainte-Cécile), 7
(Saint-Arsène and Marie-Favery) and 9 (Saint-Gabriel-Lalemant) for 2025-2026, where 1 is most
advantaged, 10 most disadvantaged, and 8 to 10 is the official *milieu défavorisé*. Only
Saint-Gabriel-Lalemant falls inside that band. All five sit in decile 8 or 9 on the SFR, the
low-income-threshold index, which is the more volatile of the two. The IMSE is built from the
enrolled pupils' parents' education and employment, not from test results, and Quebec publishes no
academic ranking of elementary schools.

The interesting part is where the school indices and the census agree and where they do not. At
Saint-Gabriel-Lalemant they agree: the most deprived index of the five sits over the zone with the
lowest median household income in @tbl-people, in the second decile. At Hélène-Boullé they diverge
in the opposite direction — a mid-range index over the most advantaged zone of the five, ninth
decile for income and third for low income. A school's index describes the families who enrol, not
the households who live within a kilometre of it, and in a borough where gentrifying blocks sit
beside older low-income pockets a catchment can draw from quite different streets than a circle
does. Nothing in the data settles which explanation applies to any one of them.

# The zone

The zone is a circle of one kilometre around 8050 avenue de Gaspé, a stand-in for the catchment
polygon that exists only in the service centre's finder and PDF maps. The Sainte-Cécile circle
overlaps this one substantially; Saint-Gabriel-Lalemant, Marie-Favery and Saint-Arsène sit further
out and overlap less.

    var el = document.createElement('div');
    el.style.cssText = style;
    if (text) { el.textContent = text; }

The red pin is École Hélène-Boullé and the solid circle its kilometre; grey pins are the four
comparators. M squares are métro stations and R squares REM stations: the whole island network is
on the map, with the three stations inside the kilometre drawn solid and the rest faint, so zooming
out shows where this corner of Villeray sits on the network. Drag and zoom to explore; the map does
not zoom on scroll.

## Reading the table

Of the five zones this one is the most advantaged on the census measures: the highest median
household income, the lowest low-income rate and the lowest share of residents in materially
deprived areas. It also has the fewest residents and the fewest dwellings, which is what a circle
containing 35 ha of parkland rather than housing produces. Children are scarce by island standards
here as everywhere in the centre, though less so than around Sainte-Cécile. The contrast worth
noting is Saint-Gabriel-Lalemant, barely 1.5 km away toward Parc-Extension, where median income is
in the second decile against this zone's ninth — a reminder of how fast the picture changes inside
Villeray. French at home is high across all five.

## Reading the table

This is where Hélène-Boullé's kilometre departs most clearly from its neighbours. Its total
incident rate is the lowest of the five and close to the island median, where Sainte-Cécile,
Saint-Arsène and Saint-Gabriel-Lalemant all sit in the eighth decile. The violent-crime line is
the sharpest difference: decile 4 here against decile 10 at Sainte-Cécile, a rate less than half
its neighbour's a kilometre down the same avenue. Break-ins and mischief follow the same pattern.
The pedestrian and cyclist line is still in the eighth decile — this is a dense grid with arterials
— but at well under half the rate recorded around Sainte-Cécile and Saint-Arsène. Marie-Favery is
the closest of the four to this zone's profile.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## What these two datasets cannot say

The city states the incident file is not official SPVM statistics; positions are moved to the
nearest intersection and 17% of incidents have no coordinates and are absent from the rates.
The collision extract ends in 2021; its last two years are pandemic years. Both are rates of
reported events, not of risk.
:::

## Reading the tables

Plexes dominate more here than in any of the comparator zones — 57% of dwellings, in the ninth
decile — with single-family houses near-absent and a median building dating from the late 1930s.
Assessed values and 2026 tax bills sit in the eighth and ninth deciles, above the island median
but below Sainte-Cécile on every property type, and well above the two zones nearer
Parc-Extension. The effective tax rate is flat at about two-thirds of a percent across all five,
so the differences in bills track assessments rather than any borough's rate. Assessed values
reflect the July 2024 market and lag transactions by roughly eighteen months.
:::

Parks are this zone's strongest line, and it is one park that does it: **parc Jarry**, 35 ha,
whose edge is **193 m** from the school door — nearer than for any school reported in this project
so far. It alone carries the zone to the ninth decile for park share and the seventh for park area
per resident, against neighbours in the first and second. Smaller spaces follow further out: parc
Villeray (965 m), parc Saint-Roch (844 m).

Rapid transit is strong but one-sided: three orange-line stations fall inside the kilometre — Jarry
at 349 m, De Castelnau at 909 m and Crémazie at 986 m — so the line is walkable, but there is no
second line within the circle.

## Listings expire

These are the 3+ bedroom listings found on 2026-10-08 within about a kilometre of 8050 avenue de
Gaspé, chosen for variety of type rather than as a sample; prices are asking prices, and the
section is not refreshed when the post is republished. Centris and Realtor.ca both refuse
individual listing pages to anything that is not a browser, so every figure here comes from a
search-result snippet and is marked *unverified*. Rentals turn over fast and some of these may
already be let. Bedroom counts are given only where a snippet stated them —
for a plex the number that matters is the bedrooms in the unit the owner would occupy, not in the
building. For a durable benchmark use the assessed values in @tbl-cost.
:::

# Sources and caveats

- **School facts**: the CSSDM pages linked in the footnotes, opened 2026-10-08. The school's own
  domain returns HTTP 403 to every automated request, including with a browser User-Agent, so the
  program, projet éducatif and admission wording are *unverified*, taken from search-index
  extracts. The triennial plan, the funding page and the Radio-Canada report did load; the
  occupancy, capacity, whole-building and gymnasium facts come from them and are verified.
- **Community links**: searched for all five schools on 2026-10-08, and *unverified* throughout —
  every school domain returns 403 to an automated request, and neither Facebook page was opened.
  For Hélène-Boullé, two of the four found are given without a hyperlink because the server answers
  an automated check for them with 404. Where a link sits on the school's own domain, that domain is
  what ties it to the right school; the two Facebook pages and the Fondation des élèves de Montréal
  page are outside it and were matched by name, borough and the school they describe. Four of the
  five have a conseil d'établissement page and an OPP; Sainte-Cécile's OPP and Marie-Favery's
  school-and-OPP page are the only Facebook presences found, Saint-Arsène's schoolyard project is
  the only outside-charity link, and no school of the five has a fondation of its own.
- **IMSE/SFR**: MEQ, *Indices de défavorisation*, Données Québec, school year 2025-2026. The MEQ
  index file counts 277 pupils where the CSSDM's triennial plan declares 351 for the same year;
  this report quotes both rather than choosing.
- **Zone tables**: `scripts/zone_stats.py` on open data fetched between 2026-09-18 and 2026-10-07
  (Ville de Montréal, Données Québec, INSPQ, Statistics Canada 2021 Census); 57 dissemination areas
  for Hélène-Boullé, 65 for Sainte-Cécile, 82 for Saint-Arsène, 73 for Saint-Gabriel-Lalemant and
  79 for Marie-Favery, assigned by centroid; the IEMV covers 100% of residents in all five zones
  and tax bills matched for 99.8% to 99.9% of units. Census 2021 is five years old; assessed values
  reflect the July 2024 market.
- **Parks and stations named above**: Ville de Montréal *espaces verts* and OpenStreetMap, with
  distances measured from the school point in the same run.
- **Listings**: as seen on Centris.ca on 2026-10-08, from search-result snippets.
- **Deciles**: among 229 in-scope schools, from `data/derived/zone_stats_all.parquet`.

# Conclusion

Four readings, in the order a parent weighs them. Each states what the tables show, not a verdict.

**School.** Hélène-Boullé is an ordinary neighbourhood school with no selective stream and no
application gate — admission is by address, in a January window (@tbl-school-hb). It is full: 100%
occupancy against a capacity of 391, with the CSSDM's own forecasts easing over the next two years.
An expansion was built around 2020-22; the gymnasium that went with it was not funded, was refused
at PQI 2024-2034, resubmitted for 2025-2035, and does not appear in the 2026-2036 list. IMSE decile
5 and SFR decile 8 — a socioeconomic index of enrolled pupils, not a measure of academic
performance.

The four comparators differ from it in ways no zone table shows (@tbl-school-sc, @tbl-school-sa,
@tbl-school-sgl, @tbl-school-mf). Saint-Arsène is the only one with a selective gate, and it covers
one stream rather than the school. Marie-Favery is designated for integrating pupils with a physical
disability and runs a specialised class for 4- and 5-year-olds. Saint-Gabriel-Lalemant is the only
one in the official *milieu défavorisé* band, and its annexe sits between a completed demolition and
an unfunded phase two. Sainte-Cécile has the newest schoolyard of the five and its own report.

**Safety.** The clearest point of difference. This kilometre reports the lowest crime rate of the
five compared, near the island median, with violent crime at decile 4 against decile 10 a kilometre
south at Sainte-Cécile (@tbl-safety). Pedestrian and cyclist victims remain in the eighth decile.
Both datasets count reported events with known coverage gaps.

**Livability.** The most advantaged census picture of the five, on income, low-income rate and
material deprivation, with high French-at-home and high turnover (@tbl-people, @tbl-indices). Parc
Jarry at 193 m is the standout, and Jarry station at 349 m puts the orange line within a short walk
(@tbl-parks). Children remain scarce by island standards.

**Affordability.** Plex-dominated prewar stock, 57% plex units, almost no houses; assessed values
and tax bills in the eighth and ninth deciles — above the island median, below Sainte-Cécile, above
the zones toward Parc-Extension (@tbl-stock, @tbl-cost). The month's listings are consistent with
that, though lightly verified (@tbl-for-sale, @tbl-for-rent).

Next steps for this school:

1. **Confirm the catchment** on the CSSDM finder for candidate addresses; the circle is a stand-in,
   and Sainte-Cécile's zone overlaps this one.
2. **Ask about the gymnasium and the squeeze on space** — whether the PQI 2025-2035 request
   succeeded, where physical education happens meanwhile, and what 100% occupancy means for class
   sizes and the schoolyard. The conseil d'établissement and the OPP in @tbl-school-hb are the places
   to ask.
3. **Watch the January registration window**, which ran 7 to 27 January for the 2026-2027 year.
4. **What this report does not yet cover**: childcare places, transit frequency, heat islands,
   rents by CMHC zone, and the secondary school the zone feeds.

::: {.callout-important}
## Bottom line

Hélène-Boullé's kilometre is the quietest and greenest of the five compared — lowest crime, parc
Jarry across the street, the orange line a short walk — and its housing costs sit just below its
nearest neighbour's while staying well above the island median. The thing to verify before acting
is inside the school rather than around it: it is at 100% of capacity and its gymnasium project has
been refused once and resubmitted, with no published outcome.
:::
